text: This software is insanely expensive. They want $500 for a lifetime license.
The user interface isn't as good as prusaslicer
I hate that I have to import into a slicer to check fit when cutting in grid mode.
Please tell me there's an easy way to use prusaslicer
or that a feature like this will be available soon.
What it doesn't let you do is split it along multiple planes simultaneously, or using a grid.
Instead I have to repeat the process multiple times and risk screwing something up in the process.
I can't just tell it my printer's build volume and then have it decide cut lines
In short the cut tool in prusaslicer is only useful if you are cutting something into no more than 3 parts.
I have to cut some things into 18-20 and that's just too much of a headache.
While the LuBan's $500 price tag may be daunting
alternatives like Meshmixer, TinkerCAD, or Fusion 360 may be more affordable
Splitting files and adding connectors is already supported by Prusa Slicer
It's not too hard up to a dozen or so parts
for most that cannot be done in PrusaSlicer I would use a combination of Gimp and OpenSCAD.
